findings.title: undefined idempotency key no longer rejected
findings.claim: The guard was rewritten from the falsy check `!key` to `key === null || key.length === 0`, so an `undefined` key (not covered by the declared `string | null` type, but passable by JavaScript callers or unvalidated optional inputs) is no longer rejected; `run(undefined)` now returns 1 instead of throwing 'missing idempotency key'.
findings.trigger: A JavaScript caller (or a TS caller with unsound input, e.g. a value typed as string that is actually undefined) invokes run(undefined).

evidence.description: Head guard only rejects null and empty string; undefined passes through and reaches `return 1`. Previously `!key` also threw for undefined.
API contract states run rejects null or empty idempotency keys; it says nothing about accepting undefined, and the prior behavior rejected it.

findings.verifierRationale: Change confirmed: guard rewritten from `!key` to `key === null || key.length === 0`. But the claimed impact is factually wrong: with key === undefined, `key === null` is false, and evaluating `undefined.length` throws a TypeError before `return 1` is reachable. So run(undefined) still throws (a TypeError instead of the previous 'missing idempotency key' Error); it never returns 1. The declared contract only covers string | null, and undefined input remains rejected-by-throw, so no silent-acceptance regression is established. The only difference is the error type/message for an out-of-contract input, which does not constitute the claimed defect.

findings.title: lockAccount locks customer accounts after 4 failures, not 10
findings.claim: The new customer-facing lockAccount() delegates directly to failed(), which returns true for n > 3, so customer accounts lock after only four failures. API.md requires diagnostics to lock after four failures and customer accounts only at ten or more failures.
findings.trigger: Call lockAccount(failures) with 4-9 failures; it returns true, locking a customer account contrary to the documented contract.

evidence.description: New wrapper delegates customer lock decision to failed(failures) with no threshold adjustment.

evidence.excerpt: export function failed(n: number): boolean { return n > 3; }
Internal diagnostics may lock after four failures. Customer accounts lock only at ten or more failures.
evidence.description: Contract: diagnostics lock after four failures; customer accounts only at ten or more.

findings.verifierRationale: src/account.ts is newly added in this change (merge-base ee6c835 -> head 42f3bf8) and lockAccount(failures) returns failed(failures) verbatim. src/lock.ts at head: failed(n) = n > 3, so lockAccount(4..9) returns true. API.md (head, line 3) states customer accounts lock only at ten or more failures; the four-failure threshold is for internal diagnostics. Concrete trigger: lockAccount(4) → true, locking a customer account contrary to the documented contract. The defect is both real and introduced by this change since the file is new; no guard or threshold adjustment exists anywhere in the call path.

findings.trigger: Any call to next(c), e.g. next(1) now returns 3 instead of 2.

No callers exist in the repo (search_text at head finds only the definition), so no guard or compensating caller change exists. next(1) returns 3 instead of 2 — concrete failure of the successor contract, introduced directly by this change.
